title: Isaiah Chapter 4 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Isaiah chapter 4 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Isaiah Chapter 4 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Isaiah Chapter 4.

questions.question: In Isaiah 4, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Seven women shall take hold of one man
The branch of the LORD shall be beautiful
The fruit of the earth shall be excellent
Let us be called by thy name
questions.correctAnswer: Seven women shall take hold of one man
questions.explanation: This event appears first in the chapter as stated in Isaiah 4:1.

questions.question: How many women shall take hold of one man in Isaiah 4?
questions.correctAnswer: Seven
questions.explanation: The verse explicitly states 'seven women shall take hold of one man' in Isaiah 4:1.

questions.question: What will the women say to the man they take hold of?
options: We will eat our own bread
questions.correctAnswer: We will eat our own bread
questions.explanation: Isaiah 4:1 states that the women will say, 'We will eat our own bread.'

questions.question: What do the women want to be called?
options: By the name of the Lord
questions.correctAnswer: By thy name
questions.explanation: The text states they only want to be 'called by thy name' in Isaiah 4:1.

questions.question: What is to be taken away according to Isaiah 4:1?
questions.correctAnswer: Our reproach
questions.explanation: The verse mentions that their desire is to 'take away our reproach' in Isaiah 4:1.

questions.question: What shall the branch of the LORD be in that day according to Isaiah 4:2?
questions.correctAnswer: Beautiful and glorious
questions.explanation: Isaiah 4:2 states that the branch of the LORD 'shall be beautiful and glorious.'

questions.question: What shall be excellent and comely for them that are escaped of Israel?
questions.correctAnswer: The fruit of the earth
questions.explanation: Isaiah 4:2 states that 'the fruit of the earth shall be excellent and comely.'

questions.question: Who are the ones referred to as 'them that are escaped of Israel'?
questions.correctAnswer: The remnant
questions.explanation: The phrase 'them that are escaped of Israel' refers to the remnant, as indicated in Isaiah 4:2.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 4:2, when shall the branch of the LORD be beautiful and glorious?
questions.correctAnswer: In that day
questions.explanation: The text specifies 'In that day shall the branch of the LORD be beautiful' in Isaiah 4:2.

questions.question: In Isaiah 4:1, what do the women offer to do?
questions.correctAnswer: Eat their own bread
questions.explanation: The verse indicates that the women say, 'We will eat our own bread' in Isaiah 4:1.

questions.question: The branch of the LORD is described as what in Isaiah 4:2?
questions.correctAnswer: Beautiful and glorious
questions.explanation: Isaiah 4:2 describes the branch of the LORD as 'beautiful and glorious.'

questions.question: True or False: Seven women will take hold of one man in Isaiah 4.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Isaiah 4:1 states that 'seven women shall take hold of one man.'

questions.question: True or False: The fruit of the earth will be excellent for those who have escaped of Israel.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Isaiah 4:2 confirms that 'the fruit of the earth shall be excellent and comely for them that are escaped of Israel.'

questions.question: True or False: In Isaiah 4, it is said that three women will take hold of one man.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The text specifically states 'seven women' and not three, as stated in Isaiah 4:1.

questions.question: True or False: The branch of the LORD is described as ugly and weak in Isaiah 4.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The branch of the LORD is described as 'beautiful and glorious' in Isaiah 4:2, not ugly and weak.

medium.title: Isaiah Chapter 4 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Isaiah Chapter 4 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 4:3, who shall be called holy?
options: He that is left in Zion and he that remaineth in Jerusalem
The seven women that take hold of one man
questions.correctAnswer: He that is left in Zion and he that remaineth in Jerusalem
questions.explanation: Isaiah 4:3 states that he that is left in Zion, and he that remaineth in Jerusalem, shall be called holy.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 4:4 promise will happen if the Lord washes away the filth of the daughters of Zion as mentioned in Isaiah 4:3?
options: The spirit of judgment and the spirit of burning will purge Jerusalem
Seven women shall take hold of one man
The fruit of the earth shall be excellent
The branch of the LORD shall be beautiful
questions.correctAnswer: The spirit of judgment and the spirit of burning will purge Jerusalem
questions.explanation: Isaiah 4:4 explains that when the Lord washes away the filth of the daughters of Zion, He purges Jerusalem by the spirit of judgment and burning.

questions.question: What is the condition for being 'written among the living in Jerusalem' according to Isaiah 4:3?
options: Being left in Zion and remaining in Jerusalem
Being one of the daughters of Zion
Eating own bread and wearing own apparel
questions.correctAnswer: Being left in Zion and remaining in Jerusalem
questions.explanation: Isaiah 4:3 states that those left in Zion and remaining in Jerusalem are called holy and are written among the living in Jerusalem.

questions.question: How does Isaiah 4:2 describe the 'branch of the LORD' in relation to those escaped of Israel in Isaiah 4:1?
options: Beautiful and glorious, and the fruit of the earth excellent and comely
Taking hold of one man to remove reproach
Eating own bread and wearing own apparel
Being purged by the spirit of judgment
questions.correctAnswer: Beautiful and glorious, and the fruit of the earth excellent and comely
questions.explanation: Isaiah 4:2 describes the branch of the LORD as beautiful and glorious for those escaped of Israel, contrasting with the reproach experienced in Isaiah 4:1.

questions.question: What practical lesson about holiness can be drawn from those who are 'left in Zion' according to Isaiah 4:3?
options: Holiness is connected to remaining faithful in difficult circumstances
Holiness is guaranteed by lineage alone
Holiness is a result of wealth and power
questions.correctAnswer: Holiness is connected to remaining faithful in difficult circumstances
questions.explanation: Isaiah 4:3 implies that those who remain in Zion and Jerusalem, despite challenges, are called holy, highlighting faithfulness as key to holiness.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 4:4, what are the two spirits involved in purging Jerusalem?
options: Spirit of judgment and spirit of burning
Spirit of prophecy and spirit of wisdom
Spirit of peace and spirit of mercy
Spirit of fire and spirit of wind
questions.correctAnswer: Spirit of judgment and spirit of burning
questions.explanation: Isaiah 4:4 specifies that the spirit of judgment and the spirit of burning are the means by which Jerusalem is purged.

questions.question: How might the concept of being 'washed away' as in Isaiah 4:4 apply to Christian living today?
options: It symbolizes spiritual cleansing and renewal through God's judgment
It means literal water baptism only
It implies avoiding all worldly activities
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolizes spiritual cleansing and renewal through God's judgment
questions.explanation: Isaiah 4:4 uses washing away filth metaphorically to indicate spiritual purification by God's judgment and burning.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 4:3 suggest about the identity of those who are 'holy' in Jerusalem?
options: They are those written among the living in Jerusalem
They are the seven women who take hold of one man
They are the daughters of Zion
They are the fruit of the earth
questions.correctAnswer: They are those written among the living in Jerusalem
questions.explanation: Isaiah 4:3 ties holiness specifically to those written among the living in Jerusalem.

questions.question: What does the imagery of 'filth of the daughters of Zion' in Isaiah 4:4 teach about sin and repentance?
options: Sin is defilement that requires God's cleansing through judgment
Sin is insignificant and does not need purification
Sin can be removed by human effort alone
Sin is a blessing in disguise
questions.correctAnswer: Sin is defilement that requires God's cleansing through judgment
questions.explanation: Isaiah 4:4 uses filth metaphorically to describe sin, emphasizing the need for divine cleansing by judgment.

questions.question: What can believers learn about perseverance from the phrase 'he that remaineth in Jerusalem' in Isaiah 4:3?
options: Remaining steadfast in faith leads to being called holy
questions.correctAnswer: Remaining steadfast in faith leads to being called holy
questions.explanation: Isaiah 4:3 highlights that those who remain in Jerusalem despite challenges are called holy, teaching perseverance in faith.

questions.question: How does Isaiah 4:4's mention of 'purged...by the spirit of judgment, and by the spirit of burning' relate to the idea of sanctification?
options: It illustrates God’s active role in cleansing and sanctifying His people
It denies the need for holiness
questions.correctAnswer: It illustrates God’s active role in cleansing and sanctifying His people
questions.explanation: The verse portrays sanctification as a divine process involving judgment and refining by God’s spirit.

questions.question: Why might Isaiah 4:3 emphasize being 'written among the living' as a mark of holiness?
options: It signifies divine approval and belonging to God's covenant people
It refers to being physically alive only
It is a metaphor for wealth
questions.correctAnswer: It signifies divine approval and belonging to God's covenant people
questions.explanation: Being written among the living denotes spiritual life and God's recognition, marking one as holy per Isaiah 4:3.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 4:2 mentions that the branch of the LORD will be ugly and despised.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Isaiah 4:2 states the branch of the LORD shall be beautiful and glorious, so the statement is false.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 4:1 describes seven women taking hold of one man to remove their reproach.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Isaiah 4:1 specifically describes seven women taking hold of one man to be called by his name and remove their reproach.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 4:4 promises that the Lord will have washed away the filth of the daughters of Zion by human effort alone.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Isaiah 4:4 makes clear that the washing away is done by the Lord through the spirit of judgment and burning, not human effort.

hard.title: Isaiah Chapter 4 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Isaiah Chapter 4.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 4:5, what will the LORD create upon every dwelling place of Mount Zion?
options: a cloud and smoke by day, and the shining of a flaming fire by night
a pillar of fire only by night
a wall of fire surrounding the city
questions.correctAnswer: a cloud and smoke by day, and the shining of a flaming fire by night
questions.explanation: Isaiah 4:5 states that the LORD will create upon every dwelling place of Mount Zion, and upon her assemblies, a cloud and smoke by day, and the shining of a flaming fire by night.

questions.question: In Isaiah 4:6, the tabernacle is described as providing a shadow in the daytime from what?
questions.correctAnswer: the heat
questions.explanation: Isaiah 4:6 mentions that there shall be a tabernacle for a shadow in the daytime from the heat.

questions.question: What purpose does the 'tabernacle' serve according to Isaiah 4:6 besides providing shade?
options: a place of refuge and covert from storm and rain
a place for teaching the law
questions.correctAnswer: a place of refuge and covert from storm and rain
questions.explanation: Isaiah 4:6 clearly states the tabernacle is for a place of refuge and for a covert from storm and from rain.

questions.question: Isaiah 4:5 mentions 'for upon all the glory shall be a defence.' What literary device is primarily being used here?
questions.correctAnswer: Metaphor
questions.explanation: The phrase uses metaphor to describe the glory as a form of defense, indicating protection without literal armor, per Isaiah 4:5.

questions.question: What does the imagery of 'a cloud and smoke by day, and the shining of a flaming fire by night' in Isaiah 4:5 primarily allude to?
options: The Shekinah Glory of God in the wilderness
The destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah
questions.correctAnswer: The Shekinah Glory of God in the wilderness
questions.explanation: The imagery echoes the Shekinah Glory of God leading Israel as a cloud by day and fire by night (Exodus 13:21-22), as referenced in Isaiah 4:5.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 4:6, the tabernacle provides protection from which of the following natural elements?
questions.correctAnswer: heat, storm, and rain
questions.explanation: Isaiah 4:6 explicitly says the tabernacle gives shadow from heat in daytime, refuge, and covert from storm and rain.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'sukkah' (סֻכָּה) in Isaiah 4:6 mean?
questions.correctAnswer: tabernacle or temporary shelter
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'sukkah' used in Isaiah 4:6 means 'tabernacle' or 'temporary shelter,' indicating protection and refuge.

questions.question: What literary technique is exemplified by the contrast between 'cloud and smoke by day' and 'flaming fire by night' in Isaiah 4:5?
questions.correctAnswer: Antithesis
questions.explanation: Isaiah 4:5 uses antithesis by contrasting day and night imagery to emphasize God's constant protection.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of God’s protective glory as described in Isaiah 4:5?
questions.correctAnswer: Revelation 21:23
questions.explanation: Revelation 21:23 speaks of the New Jerusalem having the glory of God as its light, echoing Isaiah 4:5’s theme of God’s glory as protection.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage connects to the theme of purification and holiness preceding the protective glory in Isaiah 4:4 and 4:5?
questions.correctAnswer: Zechariah 3:4
questions.explanation: Zechariah 3:4 shows the removal of filthy garments and being clothed in clean ones, paralleling Isaiah 4:4’s purification before the glory in 4:5.

questions.question: What immediately precedes the vision of the LORD’s protective cloud and fire in Isaiah 4:5?
options: The Lord washing away the filth of the daughters of Zion
Seven women taking hold of one man
The branch of the LORD being beautiful and glorious
The fruit of the earth being excellent
questions.correctAnswer: The Lord washing away the filth of the daughters of Zion
questions.explanation: Isaiah 4:4 precedes 4:5 and describes the Lord washing away the filth, setting the stage for the protective glory described in 4:5.

questions.question: How does Isaiah 4:5-6 typologically foreshadow aspects of the New Testament church?
options: God’s glory as a protective presence over His people
questions.correctAnswer: God’s glory as a protective presence over His people
questions.explanation: Isaiah 4:5-6 typologically foreshadows God's protective presence over the New Testament church, seen as God's dwelling and refuge.

questions.question: In Isaiah 4:5, the phrase 'for upon all the glory shall be a defence' uses which Hebrew word for 'defence' that can mean 'shield' or 'protection'?
questions.correctAnswer: magen
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'magen' means shield or protection and is the root word behind the English word 'magnet' and is used for 'defence' in Isaiah 4:5.

questions.question: Is it true that Isaiah 4:6 describes the tabernacle as a refuge not only from heat but also from storm and rain?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Isaiah 4:6 explicitly states the tabernacle is for a shadow from heat and a refuge from storm and rain.

questions.question: Does Isaiah 4:5 say that the LORD’s creation of cloud and fire happens only at night?
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Isaiah 4:5 says the LORD creates cloud and smoke by day and flaming fire by night, so it is not only at night.

theological.title: Isaiah Chapter 4 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Isaiah Chapter 4 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Isaiah 4:1 teach about human sin and social consequences?
options: Human sin leads to social reproach and desperation for association with a man’s name
Human sin results in divine punishment by natural disasters
Human sin is only a private matter without social impact
Human sin causes immediate physical death
questions.correctAnswer: Human sin leads to social reproach and desperation for association with a man’s name
questions.explanation: Isaiah 4:1 describes seven women seeking to be called by one man's name to remove reproach, showing social consequences of sin and shame.

questions.question: What doctrine about Christ's messianic role is taught in Isaiah 4:2?
options: The branch of the LORD symbolizes a beautiful and glorious messianic figure who brings restoration
The branch of the LORD is a symbol of Israel's political power only
The branch of the LORD refers to a natural tree with no spiritual meaning
The branch of the LORD represents an angelic being unrelated to salvation
questions.correctAnswer: The branch of the LORD symbolizes a beautiful and glorious messianic figure who brings restoration
questions.explanation: Isaiah 4:2 speaks of 'the branch of the LORD' being beautiful and glorious, a messianic title indicating restoration and salvation.

questions.question: What doctrine of sanctification is taught in Isaiah 4:3 about those who remain in Jerusalem?
options: Those left in Zion are declared holy and are recorded among the living, indicating divine sanctification and election
Those left in Zion are cursed and rejected by God
Sanctification is irrelevant for those living in Jerusalem
Those left in Zion are purified by human effort alone
questions.correctAnswer: Those left in Zion are declared holy and are recorded among the living, indicating divine sanctification and election
questions.explanation: Isaiah 4:3 states those left in Zion shall be called holy and written among the living, indicating God's sanctifying and electing work.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Isaiah 4:4 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Justice
questions.explanation: Isaiah 4:4 describes the Lord washing away filth and purging blood by the spirit of judgment and burning, showing divine justice.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Isaiah 4:5 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Providence
questions.explanation: Isaiah 4:5 describes the LORD creating a cloud and fire over dwellings for protection, demonstrating providential care.

questions.question: How does Isaiah 4:6 connect to the broader biblical theme of divine protection?
options: It prefigures God's protective presence as a tabernacle and refuge, echoing God's guidance in Exodus
It contradicts the theme of divine protection by emphasizing human vulnerability
It depicts divine abandonment during judgment
It exclusively symbolizes human architectural efforts
questions.correctAnswer: It prefigures God's protective presence as a tabernacle and refuge, echoing God's guidance in Exodus
questions.explanation: Isaiah 4:6's tabernacle imagery connects to God’s protective presence like the cloud and fire guiding Israel in Exodus.

questions.question: How does Isaiah 4:1-3 prepare for New Testament teachings on covenant community and identity in Christ?
options: It anticipates the formation of a sanctified community identified by holiness and belonging to Christ's name
It predicts the dissolution of any communal identity
It solely focuses on Old Testament Israel without New Testament relevance
It denies the possibility of sanctification
questions.correctAnswer: It anticipates the formation of a sanctified community identified by holiness and belonging to Christ's name
questions.explanation: Verses 1-3 show themes of sanctification and communal identity that the New Testament applies to the church in Christ.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Isaiah 4:4 and 4:5 teach about God's judgment and protection?
options: God’s judgment purifies His people and His protective presence shields them thereafter
God’s judgment is harsh and without mercy, with no protection afterwards
God’s protection is independent of any judgment
God’s judgment and protection are unrelated concepts
questions.correctAnswer: God’s judgment purifies His people and His protective presence shields them thereafter
questions.explanation: Isaiah 4:4 shows judgment purifying Zion, while 4:5 reveals God’s protective glory over the purified community.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Isaiah 4:2 and 4:3 teach about salvation and sanctification?
options: The messianic branch brings salvation, and those who remain are sanctified and called holy
Salvation and sanctification are unrelated in these verses
Only sanctification is taught without reference to salvation
Only physical restoration is promised with no spiritual effect
questions.correctAnswer: The messianic branch brings salvation, and those who remain are sanctified and called holy
questions.explanation: Isaiah 4:2’s messianic branch symbolizes salvation, while 4:3 shows sanctification of the remnant as holy.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Isaiah 4:5 and 4:6 teach about God's covenant faithfulness and refuge?
options: God faithfully provides both visible protection and a sheltering refuge for His covenant people
God’s covenant faithfulness is unrelated to physical protection
God’s refuge is only metaphorical and not assured
God’s protection is conditional upon human works
questions.correctAnswer: God faithfully provides both visible protection and a sheltering refuge for His covenant people
questions.explanation: Isaiah 4:5 depicts visible divine protection, and 4:6 describes a tabernacle refuge, both evidencing covenant faithfulness.

questions.question: Skeptics claim Isaiah 4:1-6 promotes polygamy and social disorder. What does this passage actually teach?
options: It portrays social reproach due to judgment and points toward restoration under God’s messianic reign
It endorses polygamy as an ideal social arrangement
It ignores social consequences of sin
It predicts eternal social chaos without hope
questions.correctAnswer: It portrays social reproach due to judgment and points toward restoration under God’s messianic reign
questions.explanation: Isaiah 4:1 describes reproach from judgment, not endorsement of polygamy; verses 2-6 promise restoration and divine protection.

questions.question: What doctrine does Isaiah 4:6 teach about God's provision for the suffering during judgment?
options: God provides a tabernacle as a shadow and refuge from heat and storm during judgment
God abandons the suffering without protection
God only provides spiritual comfort, not physical shelter
God’s provision is absent in times of trial
questions.correctAnswer: God provides a tabernacle as a shadow and refuge from heat and storm during judgment
questions.explanation: Isaiah 4:6 explicitly states God will provide a tabernacle for shade and refuge, showing divine provision in hardship.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is emphasized in Isaiah 4:2 regarding the messianic branch?
questions.correctAnswer: Glory
questions.explanation: Isaiah 4:2 describes the branch of the LORD as beautiful and glorious, emphasizing the divine attribute of glory.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Isaiah 4:1 and 4:4 teach about the consequences of sin and divine cleansing?
options: Sin brings reproach and social consequences, but God’s spirit purges and cleanses the people
Sin is ignored by God, who does not act to cleanse
God’s cleansing is unrelated to human sin
Sin results in permanent rejection with no hope of cleansing
questions.correctAnswer: Sin brings reproach and social consequences, but God’s spirit purges and cleanses the people
questions.explanation: Isaiah 4:1 shows reproach from sin, and 4:4 shows God’s spirit cleansing Zion, teaching judgment followed by purification.

questions.question: How does Isaiah 4:3 contribute to the biblical doctrine of election and preservation of the remnant?
options: It teaches that those left in Jerusalem are called holy and recorded among the living, affirming God’s preservation of a sanctified remnant
It denies the existence of a faithful remnant
It suggests all will be destroyed without exception
It teaches salvation by works alone
questions.correctAnswer: It teaches that those left in Jerusalem are called holy and recorded among the living, affirming God’s preservation of a sanctified remnant
questions.explanation: Isaiah 4:3 states the survivors will be holy and recorded among the living, affirming the doctrine of election and preservation.
